title: Google's AI note-taking app transcribes your meetings completely offline
key_facts: Google released Google AI Edge Foresight, an experimental Mac note-taking app that works completely offline.
It uses the on-device EmbeddingGemma 2 model, which TechCrunch says has 740 million parameters, and is free (per The Verge).
Users can type shorthand notes while it transcribes; the app turns them into polished notes based on the transcript.
A built-in assistant answers questions about the meeting; users can upload documents (PDFs, Google Docs, Office files, Markdown, bookmarks) as a knowledge base.
Google says files, audio and notes never leave the computer (per The Verge).
Optimised for Apple Silicon Macs; competes with Granola, and TechCrunch notes Wispr, Calendly and Superhuman (via Fathom) also have note-takers.
quote_evidence: The Mac app can work completely offline, utilizing the on-device EmbeddingGemma 2 model, with 740 million parameters, to capture meeting notes across apps, including those from in-person meetings.
Google says your files, meeting audio, and notes “never leave your computer.”
why_it_matters_hint: Privacy-minded workers get AI meeting notes without audio going to a cloud service.
notes: Pool link was The Verge, which credits TechCrunch ('as reported earlier by TechCrunch'); TechCrunch read as the first reporter, Verge for the free and 'never leave' details. TechCrunch suggests the app may mainly showcase Google's offline models.
